feature: Move a title from A to B, grow it, fade it
summary: A title can fly in, grow and fade out with no forms: Animate In and Animate Out on its right-click menu, keys as white diamonds on its clip that you drag in time, and Premiere's four eases on a key's right-click.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A recording open, playhead at 0:01.

try.do: Press T, click on the frame, type a title, press Command-Return. It lands on a track called Title.
Right-click the title's clip on the timeline and choose Animate In, Slide.
At 0:02, right-click the title on the canvas and choose Animate Out, Fade.
Click the Scale diamond in Animating, step a second later, type 160 in Scale.
Right-click the diamond on the clip where the grow lands and choose Ease In and Out.
Drag the diamond where the grow starts half a second later.
Scrub from 0:01 to 0:04 and watch it fly in, grow and fade.

evaluate: Is right-click on the clip or the canvas where you would look for Animate In and Animate Out?
Do Fade, Slide, Pop and Scale feel like the four you want, and is half a second the right length?
Is one diamond per moment on the clip (all values keyed there together) right, or do you want one per value?
Does Ease In meaning 'slows as it arrives at this key' (Premiere's meaning) match what you expect?
Is a key at the very start of a clip, half hidden under the trim grip, easy enough to grab?
rough: The mock draws key marks on a clip as read-only; the task asked for diamonds you drag and right-click, so they are draggable here.
The lanes under the title (Position, Opacity, Scale) are still the old timing bars, not the mock's diamonds joined by a line (video-move-wt step 5); that is the next keyframe task's work.
The mock's 'Between the keys' easing and Straight or Curved path controls in the panel are not built; easing lives on the key's right-click.
There is no diamond on the track header to arm keying: the panel's diamond is the one stopwatch.
A preset's Out keys stay where they were written if the title is later made longer, as keys do in Premiere, so the fade can end before the title does.
A key drag between tracks or a real pointer drag of a diamond cannot be driven by a walk; the walk moves it through the app, and the gesture was checked by building it, not by hand.
